newsitem.title: FRANCE: PRESS DIGEST - France - Le Monde April 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - France - Le Monde April 24.

text.p: These are leading stories in afternoon daily Le Monde.
-- Italy refuses to be excluded from European monetary union in 1999, as forecast by the European Commission.

-- Eramet chairman Yves Rambaud calls in an interview for an industrial solution to the tensions over nickel mining in New Caledonia. He favours building a nickel smelter in northern New Caledonia, as requested by separatists, and considers transfer of mining fields to support that project.
-- Businessman Armand Frydman chosen by Nanterre court to take over children's clothing group Jacadi, placed under legal administration since October 1996.
-- Hotel group Accor posts a 1.06 billion franc profit for 1996.
-- Labour crisis intensifies at the Paris area transport authority RATP; an executive was held hostage yesterday by workers protesting against plans to eliminate night services for staff.
-- Daewoo to invest 278 million francs in refrigerator manufacturing plant in Lorraine.

-- Regional air carrier Brit Air becomes the first franchised company to join the Air France group, expected to generate some 250 million francs additional turnover for Brit Air. Air France is expected to forecast a 500 million franc profit for 1997-1998 after a board meeting today.
-- Members of the ruling coalition expect outgoing National Assembly speaker Philippe Seguin to join the Gaullist campaign for the upcoming parliamentary election.
